conclusion.justification: The report concludes that the claim is "well-supported," citing randomized trial and cohort evidence that higher olive oil consumption reduces stroke risk, despite noting some minor caveats in other analyses. Therefore, it endorses the claim.

report:
**Conclusion: The claim is well-supported, though with some nuance.** Multiple lines of evidence—randomized trial, cohort studies, and meta-analyses—converge on a protective association between olive oil consumption and stroke risk, though the effect size varies by study type and olive oil variety.

The strongest evidence comes from the PREDIMED randomized controlled trial, which found that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil reduced cardiovascular events, "particularly stroke," compared to a lower-fat control diet, with reports of roughly a 33% reduction in stroke risk in the EVOO group (https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/pdf/10.1161/hypertensionaha.113.03353; https://myhealthcare.com/Food/Olive_Oil/index.html). Because this is a randomized trial, it provides the most reliable causal evidence.

Observational cohort evidence, including the French Three-City Study and a meta-analysis by Martínez-González et al., similarly found that each 25g/day increment in olive oil intake was associated with a 24% reduction in stroke risk (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261954820_Olive_oil_consumption_and_risk_of_CHD_andor_stroke_A_meta-analysis_of_case-control_cohort_and_intervention_studies).

However, one caveat: a 2020 meta-analysis noted by Healthline found no significant link between olive oil intake and stroke risk specifically, suggesting effects may depend on population, oil type (extra-virgin vs. refined), and baseline diet (https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/11-proven-benefits-of-olive-oil).

**Bottom line:** The bulk of evidence, especially from the PREDIMED RCT, supports that higher olive oil consumption—particularly extra-virgin olive oil—reduces stroke risk, though effect sizes vary across studies and some analyses show no significant association.
